trust_decision.summary: A dashboard must require authentication whenever the operator configured a username/password, including through the pre-rename bare $USERNAME/$PASSWORD env pair; the legacy pair is adopted only when $PASSWORD is set and no newer source supplied credentials, so a lone OS-set $USERNAME never enables auth. The decision is made in DashboardSettings.parse_args and mirrored in the CLI-time _validate_credentials guard.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about configured auth env vars being ignored, and this is the only place the credential env vars are read to set using_password / password_hash, so an engineer reading the summary looks here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API resolve_credentials(username_arg, password_arg, environ) — new shared resolver called from the esphome-device-builder CLI and from DashboardSettings.parse_args
public API DashboardSettings.parse_args (esphome_device_builder/controllers/config/settings.py:100), reached from the esphome-device-builder CLI at esphome_device_builder/__main__.py:358-360
esphome-device-builder CLI command — argparse-time _validate_credentials guard invoked at esphome_device_builder/__main__.py:319
esphome-device-builder CLI startup — _warn_legacy_credential_env() called from main() at fix.diff:42

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The CLI-time validator only rejects a half-set pair and never enables authentication; once DashboardSettings.parse_args adopts the legacy pair the dashboard is protected, so the validator can keep resolving $ESPHOME_* only — its mismatch error is just a startup UX nicety.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A lone bare $USERNAME (the OS login user, always set on Windows) must never be adopted as the dashboard username: with $ESPHOME_PASSWORD or --password but no $ESPHOME_USERNAME the dashboard must stay unauthenticated and the pair must be rejected as a mismatch. An over-broad legacy fallback silently promotes the OS login name to dashboard username.

O6_input_shapes: lone bare $PASSWORD with no username (mismatch; must error, never silent auth)
lone bare $USERNAME with no $PASSWORD (never read; ignored)
bare $USERNAME + $ESPHOME_PASSWORD (new scheme supplies a password, legacy pair not adopted)
CLI --username/--password plus legacy bare pair (CLI wins)
$ESPHOME_USERNAME/$ESPHOME_PASSWORD plus legacy bare pair (new scheme wins)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another legacy env-var alias resolved inline (the $ESPHOME_REMOTE_BUILD_PORT / $ESPHOME_REMOTE_BUILD_HOST / $ESPHOME_TRUSTED_DOMAINS pattern) for an auth-adjacent option
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already resolves several legacy env vars inline one after another with a CLI-then-env precedence comment; a maintainer adding a legacy alias would copy that pattern and skip the credential resolver.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second credential deprecation-warning helper that inspects args or os.environ directly instead of calling resolve_credentials
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _warn_deprecated_credential_flags is already a standalone CLI-layer warning that inspects args itself, and the fix adds _warn_legacy_credential_env beside it; a variant that reads os.environ directly is the natural copy-paste mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dashboard credentials persisted/reloaded through the metadata sidecar and merged as another credential source
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already has a save/reload path that decodes a legacy blob with fail-safe defaults and drops legacy keys; a maintainer storing auth state there would add a merge branch in the loader rather than in the resolver.

O9_family: CWE-306 missing authentication for critical function — fail-open credential resolution (authentication silently disabled when the legacy env names are ignored)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a bare $USERNAME/$PASSWORD fallback only inside DashboardSettings.parse_args, reading $USERNAME unconditionally (breaking the lone-OS-user guard) and leaving the CLI-time _validate_credentials guard and the deprecation warning untouched.
